def: Training a small student model to imitate a larger teacher, using the teacher's probabilities or its written answers as the training signal.
In distillation, the teacher is the large trained model being imitated and the student is the smaller model being trained.
A divisor applied to logits before the softmax; values above 1 flatten the distribution so small probabilities of wrong answers become visible to the loss.
The teacher's full probability distribution over answers, used as a training target in place of a single hard label.
Distillation in which the student minimises a divergence from the teacher's next-token distribution at every position of the training text.
Distillation by sampling answers from the teacher and fine-tuning the student on that text, which needs no access to the teacher's probabilities.
Distillation in which the student generates the text and the teacher scores it, so the student learns on the kind of prefixes it will produce at test time.
Forward KL forces the student to put mass wherever the teacher does (mode-covering), while reverse KL lets it commit to one of the teacher's modes (mode-seeking).
Training data written or labelled by a model instead of a person, whose quality depends on the checks applied to it.
The loss of the rare parts of a distribution when each generation of models is trained only on the previous generation's output.
Two ways to build each generation's training set: adding synthetic data to the real data avoids collapse in the cited studies, while replacing real data with synthetic data leads to it.
